description: New York DL whose ZNB falls short of its field, layout taken from an issued credential. PII replaced.

provenance.source: PDF417 barcode decoded from a scan of the back of an issued New York driver's license (AAMVA v10, IIN 636001)
provenance.verifiedBy: Claude Code (zxing-cpp decode of the source image)
provenance.anonymization: Every identifying value was replaced with a placeholder of the same byte length, so the encoded layout is byte-for-byte unchanged: DCS/DAC/DAD (names), DAQ (customer ID), DAG/DAK (address, NY ZIP prefix kept), DCF, DBB/DBD/DBA (dates, shifted), and ZNA, which keeps the card's LAST@FIRST@MIDDLE shape. ZNB was replaced with the Ascii85 encoding of a dummy 71-byte DER structure shaped like the card's (r is 32 bytes of 0x11, s is a zero byte then 32 bytes of 0x88), so it keeps the source's 89 characters and alphabet and signs nothing. DAI (city), DDB (card revision date), DCA/DCB/DCD/DBC/DAY/DAU/DDA/DDD and the DDE/DDF/DDG truncation flags are unchanged. expectedBytes was made by writing those placeholders into the decoded symbol in place, not by running this encoder.
provenance.notes: Kept for the one thing ny-v10-dl-issued cannot show: a ZNB shorter than its field. On this card ZNB holds 89 characters and then one space. Every one of the 89 falls in Ascii85's '!'..'u' alphabet, and read that way they decode to 71 bytes that parse as a DER SEQUENCE of two INTEGERs, 32 and 33 bytes long, which is the encoding an ECDSA signature over 256-bit integers takes. DER gives an integer a leading zero byte only when its top bit is set, so such a signature runs 70 to 72 bytes and ZNB 88 to 90 characters; New York space-fills it to 90. The first vector's placeholder fills all 90 characters, which is why it could not catch the missing width. Here the input carries ZNB as a person would type it, with no trailing space, and the encoder has to restore the card's 120-byte ZN subfile on its own. Everything else matches ny-v10-dl-issued exactly: DL at offset 41 declaring 323 bytes, ZN at 364 declaring 120, 484 bytes total, jurisdiction version 04, and the width of all 27 elements. The card prints its DCF on the back as "Doc#".
